bib.title: Data-Efficient Image Recognition with Contrastive Predictive Coding

question: Can representations learned with an improved Contrastive Predictive Coding objective make image recognition data-efficient, i.e. accurate with few labels?
hypothesis: Spatially predictable representations may allow artificial systems to benefit from human-like data-efficiency.
contributions: CPC v2: revisited architecture and training, linear ImageNet Top-1 from 48.7% to 71.5%
Deep classifiers on CPC features with few labels (78% Top-5 at 1% labels), beating other semi-supervised methods and matching supervised with 2-5x fewer labels
CPC features beat supervised ResNets with all labels (+3.2% Top-1)
Transfer to PASCAL VOC 2007 detection: 76.6% mAP, above supervised pre-training

method.summary: CPC v2 pre-trains a patched ResNet-161 encoder on unlabeled ImageNet by predicting patch features in four spatial directions with an InfoNCE loss, with layer norm and heavy per-patch augmentation. The encoder is then frozen or fine-tuned under a linear probe, an 11-block ResNet classifier on 1-100% of labels, or Faster-RCNN on VOC 2007.
method.task: self-supervised image representation learning; linear classification, low-label classification, object detection transfer

datasets.name: ImageNet ILSVRC 2012 train (unlabeled)
datasets.preprocessing: resize 300x300, random 260x260 crop, 6x6 grid of 80x80 patches (stride 36), per-patch augmentation (2 AutoAugment transforms; elastic deformation/shear p=0.2; colour histogram p=0.2; Szegedy colour aug p=0.8; greyscale p=0.25)

datasets.name: ImageNet (labeled subsets)
datasets.split: hyperparameters chosen on separate ~10k held-out train images; test = ILSVRC-2012 validation set
datasets.preprocessing: same augmentation as pre-training; none at test; single crop

datasets.name: PASCAL VOC 2007
datasets.split: fine-tune on VOC 2007 train, mAP reported

models.name: CPC v2 ResNet-161 encoder (patched) + PixelCNN context
models.params: 305M (Table 1); combined model with ResNet-33 classifier over 500 million
models.architecture: ResNet-101 third stack widened to 46 blocks, 4096-d feature maps, 512-d bottleneck, layer norm; masked conv context network; linear predictors

other.latents: [6,6,4096] pretrain; 14x14 grid on full 224 image for classification

models.name: CPC v2 ResNet-50
models.architecture: ResNet-50 trained with CPC v2 objective

models.name: ResNet-33 classifier on CPC features
models.architecture: 11-block ResNet, 4096-d hiddens, 1024-d bottleneck, dropout before final linear

models.name: BigBiGAN, AMDIM
models.architecture: representations evaluated by the authors with a ResNet-33 on top

training.objective: InfoNCE over spatial predictions (4 directions, linear predictors), negatives from other locations and other images in the minibatch; cross-entropy for classification; Faster-RCNN loss for detection
training.optimizer: CPC pre-training: Adam beta1=0.8, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8; linear probe: Adam; supervised/classifier: SGD; encoder fine-tuning: Adam
training.lr: CPC 0.0004; linear classification 0.0005; supervised SGD searched in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2}
training.batch_size: 512 (32 workers) for CPC; 512 over 16 workers for linear; supervised per-worker batch in {16, 32}
training.epochs: 200 (CPC pre-training); fine-tuning 'a small number of epochs (chosen by cross-validation)'
training.regularisation: Polyak averaging decay 0.9999; gradient clip max norm 0.01; layer norm; smaller lr and early stopping when fine-tuning the encoder

other.pixelCNN: 5 residual blocks with 256 channels (appendix A code)

inference.samples: single crop at test; single run per setting, no seeds stated

metrics.name: Top-1 / Top-5 accuracy
metrics.definition: ImageNet ILSVRC-2012 validation set, single crop

metrics.name: mAP
metrics.definition: mean average precision on PASCAL VOC 2007

metrics.name: gain in data-efficiency
metrics.definition: factor fewer labels at which CPC classifier matches the supervised pixel baseline

eval.protocol: Linear probe, efficient classification (frozen then fine-tuned) and VOC transfer; hyperparameters picked on ~10k held-out train images; no seeds or error bars; Fig 3 ablations use a custom validation set.

limits: Comparison is between model classes; CPC stack has over 500M parameters vs about 60M for ResNet-200 (authors verified a supervised ResNet-161+33 matches ResNet-200)
Label-propagation comparison is imperfect: those methods use different architectures and assume all unlabeled images belong to one category
Ablation accuracies are on a custom validation set, not comparable to official results
No seeds, error bars, compute or wall-clock reported; BigBiGAN and AMDIM evaluated frozen only
Architectures across Table 1 differ, so apples-to-apples comparison is hard
